source.title: MechRL: Reinforcement Learning Agents Perform Circuit Discovery for Mechanistic Interpretability

record.tranche_reason: The study discovers an IOI circuit in GPT-2 small using RL edge pruning and causal-patching faithfulness, a different method from the original IOI circuit analysis. It reports IOI circuit faithfulness and size, but does not establish the original circuit's head classes or roles.
record.gate_note: The IOI results in Table 4 bear on circuit faithfulness and size. The paper reports IOI as an aggregate behavior with four surface-form variants, without variant-specific results. Other behaviors' results and the candidate-set ceiling values are not IOI outcomes. The cited original IOI circuit findings are not new results from this study.
record.test_reason: IOI is one of twelve training benchmarks for an RL circuit-discovery method (MechRL). Its IOI results (Table 4) are the method's own faithfulness and edge counts, compared with ACDC and EAP-IG greedy. The study does not identify the IOI head classes or roles and reports no component recovery for IOI; Table 3 covers held-out behaviours only. It runs no name-mover ablation and no overlap with the Wang et al. circuit. It also does not evaluate the original circuit under different ablations or metrics. These are method-performance results, not tests of any version.
record.authors_conclusion: The paraphrase is essentially right. The authors conclude that a single RL policy trained on twelve behaviours (including IOI) finds faithful circuits and transfers to held-out behaviours. A warm start shrinks the transferred circuits. The policy does not match per-behaviour search on circuit size or cost, and the attribution prefilter is the main limitation.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses an RL policy to prune an EAP-IG-prefiltered edge graph and evaluates the resulting subgraph using causal-patching KL faithfulness. The original IOI study manually identifies and evaluates a component-level circuit and its head classes and roles.
record.method_sensitivity: For IOI, EAP-IG greedy reports different circuit sizes using logit-difference versus KL attribution (1000 versus 1500 edges), with f = 0.91 in both entries. MechRL and ACDC also report different circuit sizes and faithfulness values.

fits_no_version.finding: At the edge level with KL-normalised faithfulness, faithful IOI circuits in GPT-2 small range from 211 edges (ACDC) to 1000–1500 edges (EAP-IG greedy). The authors group IOI with behaviours where attribution-greedy needs most of the candidate set.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: In edge-level graphs, faithful IOI circuits in GPT-2 small are diffuse, and their size depends strongly on the discovery method.

record.problems: The IOI results are aggregate across four variants, with no variant-specific values. The study does not report IOI-specific necessity or specificity controls in the presented results, and it does not identify whether its IOI circuit recovers the claimed head classes or roles. The discovery search is restricted to the top K = 3000 EAP-IG candidate edges.
record.rows_left_out: Results for non-IOI behaviors, including the held-out circuit validity battery in Table 3, are omitted because they do not report IOI outcomes. The policy-versus-score-ranked comparison in Figure 4b is also omitted: it compares the study's own selection with its prefilter ranking rather than testing the claimed IOI head classes or roles.

untested.parts: The study never checks its IOI circuit for the 26 heads, 7 classes, their roles, or the original faithfulness, completeness and minimality criteria. No IOI component recovery is reported.
No name-mover ablation and no measure of backup-head self-repair.
Only GPT-2 small is used. Other models, sizes, checkpoints and component reuse are not examined.
Methods are compared on size and faithfulness only. No overlap with the original circuit or between methods is reported.
The original circuit is never evaluated under alternative ablations, metrics or prompt distributions.
The four IOI frame variants are reported only in aggregate. There are no name-order, more-name or per-template results.

record.verdict_notes: IOI is a benchmark only. Table 3's component-recovery and necessity/specificity checks cover held-out behaviours, not IOI. Figure 4b/c include IOI but compare the policy with its own prefilter ranking, so they are not tests of the claim. The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V1/V5/V6 labels are removed.

versions.untested_parts: The study does not report whether its IOI circuit contains the claimed 26 attention heads in 7 classes, whether those classes perform their stated roles, or whether it passes the original faithfulness, completeness, and minimality criteria. Its own circuit is evaluated by its faithfulness metric and compared in size with other discovery methods.
No ablation of the main name-mover heads or measurement of backup-head self-repair is reported.

All experiments use GPT-2 small. The study does not test whether the same IOI head classes and roles occur in other models, sizes, or checkpoints, or whether the IOI components are reused for other tasks.

The study compares circuit sizes and faithfulness from different discovery methods, but does not compare circuit overlap or whether other ablation types and evaluation metrics recover essentially the same components.

The IOI comparison includes attribution-based circuits produced using logit-difference and KL attribution, but does not vary the IOI evaluation ablation type or prompt distribution, and does not directly measure how much of IOI behavior the original circuit explains.
The study includes four IOI surface-form variants, reported only in aggregate. It does not test IOI prompts with more than two names or separately report results by name order or template.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: MechRL policy pruned edges from the EAP-IG-prefiltered candidate graph; circuit scored by causal-patching faithfulness.
rows.note: The reported IOI result is aggregate; no variant-specific faithfulness values are given.
rows.check: This is the study's own method's IOI faithfulness (0.96) under its KL metric, aggregated over four variants. It says nothing about the 26-head, 7-class circuit or the original criteria (V1). Without per-variant results it cannot show whether the mechanism is shared across prompts (V6).

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: MechRL policy pruned edges from the EAP-IG-prefiltered candidate graph.
rows.note: The circuit is larger than the ACDC IOI circuit reported in the same table; the paper says its policy does not match per-behavior search on minimality. This is not a direct test of the original circuit's head count or minimality criteria.
rows.check: This is the edge count (1123) of the study's own MechRL circuit, a method-comparison value. It is not a test of the original circuit's minimality. 'Partial' has no defined effect to be partial against.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: ACDC greedily pruned edges, selecting the smallest circuit in a threshold sweep that reached the target faithfulness.
rows.note: This comparator's size is smaller than the MechRL circuit; it does not report the original IOI head-class identities.
rows.check: This is the ACDC baseline size (211 edges), picked as the smallest over a threshold sweep: a selection value inside a method comparison. No overlap with the original circuit is reported, so it cannot bear on V4.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: ACDC greedily pruned edges, selecting the smallest circuit in a threshold sweep that reached the target faithfulness.
rows.note: The reported circuit meets the stated target.
rows.check: ACDC's faithfulness (0.90) was selected to meet the target, so it is a selection value. It is a method comparison, not an evaluation of the original circuit.

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: EAP-IG greedy selected edges by logit-difference attribution.
rows.measure: Circuit size |C|; faithfulness f in parentheses
rows.note: The result is a size-and-faithfulness comparison circuit, not a component-overlap test.
rows.check: This is the EAP-IG greedy baseline under logit-difference attribution (1000 edges, f=.91). It is a baseline for the study's method and does not evaluate the original IOI circuit's sensitivity (V5).

rows.subject: GPT-2 small
rows.operation_detail: EAP-IG greedy selected edges by KL attribution.
rows.measure: Circuit size |C|; faithfulness f in parentheses
rows.note: Compared with logit-difference attribution, this setting reports a different circuit size and the same listed faithfulness; no component overlap is reported.
rows.check: This is the EAP-IG greedy baseline under KL attribution (1500 edges, f=.91). The ld-vs-kl difference concerns discovery-method output size, not how faithful or complete the original circuit looks under different ablations or metrics.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: MechRL's IOI circuit and the IOI method comparisons in Table 4
reader_labels.reason: The study finds a faithful IOI circuit under its own metric, but its circuit is larger than ACDC's and the results do not establish the claimed 26-head, 7-class structure or roles (r1–r6).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.condition: IOI circuits produced by the reported methods and attribution metrics
reader_labels.reason: Reported IOI circuit sizes differ across methods and between EAP-IG logit-difference and KL attribution, while the EAP-IG faithfulness values listed for those two settings are both 0.91; ablation-type and prompt-distribution sensitivity are not tested (r2–r6).

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: IOI with the study's four aggregated surface-form variants
reader_labels.reason: The policy's aggregate IOI circuit reaches f = 0.96 across the reported four-variant setting; the paper provides no per-variant results and does not test prompts with more than two names (r1).
